## TL;DR

QA pass over the three data-heavy surfaces — the Control dashboard's stats
(System Resources + AI usage), the Dev page, and the two activity logs (the
live feed and the Context → History commit log) — at 375/768/1280 px, using
headless WebKit against fixtures only. Five real defects found and fixed, each
guarded by the new 15-test `stats-dev-activity-qa-browser` suite: clipped-away
PIDs in Top-processes rows, a usage-failures grid that squeezed its reason cell
to a few pixels below 860 px, mobile-only wrap for long unbroken tokens in the
activity feed, commit subjects/file paths painting over the ±counts column
in the history panel, and an artifact target's output path clipped mid-word in
the Dev meta. The rest of the Dev page needed no fix — its existing
conventions held up under stress — and the QA coverage now pins that.

## Work and rationale

I built the QA suite on the harness pattern `agents-page-qa-browser.test.ts`
(#1223) established: mount the real components in jsdom with fixtures, render
the captured markup with the real built global stylesheet plus compiled scoped
styles in headless WebKit, and require every visible element to sit inside the
viewport at 375/768/1280 while the document never widens. Each surface got a
fixture deliberately loaded with the "long" content the task calls for: a
process table with long runtimes and orphan/unverified tags, top processes
with full Bun invocation paths, a pressure warning, stray-serve chips, a
worktree-cleanup preview with long branch names, usage stats with a
38-character role name and failure reasons hundreds of characters long, dev
targets with a 44-character name, 110-character commands and log lines
containing a 100+-character unbroken path, and a 200-character unbreakable
hex token pasted into a feed error line. The fifth defect came out of
eyeballing the captured screenshots rather than trusting the audit: the Dev
page's artifact `Output` row renders a bare `<code>` (unlike `Command`, which
has a wrapping class), so a deep output path overflowed its meta cell and was
cut off at the card edge while every geometric check still passed. The fix
gives every bare `dd > code` in the dev meta `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, and
the test's code-cell list now covers `.dev-meta dd > code`.

Two interpretation decisions worth recording. First, "Stats page" is not a
page: the stats surfaces live on Mission Control (`SystemResourcePanel`,
`UsagePanel`, stat cards), and the mobile tab bar renames Control to
"Activity" — so "Stats, Dev and activity-log pages" maps to dashboard + Dev +
feed/history logs. Second, a "long unbroken token" fixture must be genuinely
unbreakable: my first feed fixture used a long file path, and WebKit happily
wrapped it at the slashes, which made the ≥720 px wrap bug invisible. The
final fixture uses a 200-character alphanumeric token, the shape a pasted
session token actually has.

## Approaches tried

The audit-first approach paid off twice. I wrote the whole suite expecting
specific failures (long card names in Dev, serve chips in the resource panel),
ran it, and let the audit tell me what actually broke — the Dev page and the
serve chips passed because sibling rules (`.dev-command`'s `overflow-wrap`,
flex shrink inside `flex-wrap` chip lists) already handled them, and the real
defects were elsewhere. Fixing only observed failures kept the diff to five
small CSS/markup changes plus the test file.

For the `.top-pid` finding, the misleading part was that the audit reported
*off-viewport* rects for elements that were visually clipped into
invisibility: `getBoundingClientRect` ignores ancestor clipping, so the PID
looked "present" to a bounding-box check while a user saw nothing. That's why
the fix restructures the row (PID as its own grid column) rather than adding a
wrap rule — the information, not just the overflow, was the defect.

## Challenges and blockers

Two test-infrastructure traps cost real time. Playwright locators auto-wait
for a missing element, so one wrong selector (`.gc-preview` — which only
renders after clicking "Clean up worktrees"; `refreshGcStatus` populates
`gcStatus`, not the preview) silently consumed the full 30 s test timeout and
looked like a hung WebKit page. `textOf` now bounds its wait at 3 s and fails
with the selector named. Second, expanding every log toggle in jsdom before
capture collapsed the failed target's log (its log auto-opens, so my toggle
flipped it shut) — seeding `localStorage` for the persisted expanded-state
keys instead of clicking made the fixture deterministic.

One process note: the session continued across a day boundary and the test
file I was working in gained a fifth block (RepoHistoryPanel coverage) from
work done outside my visible turns. Rather than fighting it, I reconciled with
it: the history panel is a legitimate reading of "activity-log page", so I
fixed the two rules its assertions needed and folded it into the QA doc.

## Key learnings

- Ellipsis hides information as effectively as it hides overflow: anything
  nested inside a `text-overflow: ellipsis` region (the PID) is invisible
  exactly when the content is longest. Structural fixes beat wrap fixes when
  the clipped thing is data.
- Breakpoints must be read against real content widths: the usage-failures
  grid's own fixed columns (~590 px) defined where it stops working, and that
  number — not the nav's mobile breakpoint — picked the 860 px stack point.
  Widths between 720 and 860 px are easy to skip because both neighbors
  "work".
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` applied only in a narrow media query is a pattern
  worth grepping for: the feed bug existed at every width above 720 px but
  was invisible in manual testing because real error lines usually contain
  break-friendly punctuation.
- Auto-waiting locators turn a missing element into a 30 s timeout that
  masquerades as a hang; bounded waits with named errors turn it into a
  one-second diagnosis.
